newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom, Lion, CHH hoist NZ shares to strong close.
newsitem.headline: Telecom, Lion, CHH hoist NZ shares to strong close.

text.p: * NZ share prices build on previous gains to end stronger
* Index driven mostly by Telecom, CHH and Lion
* Market unperturbed by political scandals
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index +13.35 at 2,376.14
356 +4 * NZSC cap index +32.95 at 5,101.15
338 -1 * NZMC .NZMC cap index +8.53 at 1,880.24
366 +4 * Volume NZ$74.3 million. +8 at 1,195
718 +10 * Other movers - -11 -9
New Zealand share prices built on the week's solid gains to end stronger, driven mostly by Telecom but also by brewer Lion Nathan and Carter Holt Harvey.
"The market is just putting on solid gains every day and on quite good volume," Tim Snedden at brokers ANZ Securities said.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended the session up 13.35 points at 2,276.14 on turnover worth NZ$74.3 million.
The market was unperturbed by ongoing political scandals surrounding junior coalition partner, New Zealand First, even though the government's one-seat majority hangs in the balance.
"I don't think it affects investment intentions at all and even if there were another election, I don't think it would change much," Snedden said.
Telecom, mid-way through the second tranche of its share buyback, ended 10 cents higher at NZ$7.18, still reversing the trend of the first tranche which saw the stock weaken.

ANZ Securities, and others, had a buy recommendaton on Telecom when it was around NZ$6.50/6.60. Telecom was gaining independently of the buyback, they said, which has struggled on occasion to attract sufficient volume.
Brokers had taken a more positive view of the longer term prospects for Telecom rather than focussing on near term competitive pressures, as Salomon Brothers did in a recent note.
Brewer Lion Nathan gained four to NZ$3.66 and forestry stock Carter Holt Harvey firmed four to NZ$3.56.
Fisher & Paykel lost 11 cents to NZ$5.00 after it said it expected continued flat earnings in the current year.
Snedden expected the market overall to build on its gains next week.
-- James Gray, Auckland newsroom + 64 9 302 1253
